skill_outcomes.skill_name: Traditional vs Behavioral Economic Theories Comparison
skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Analyze irrational economic behaviors using traditional and behavioral economic theories.
Compare Prospect Theory with Expected Utility Theory and apply it to decision-making processes.
Analyze decision-making biases and heuristics and their impact on economic decisions.
Examine the influence of emotions on decision-making processes.
Evaluate standard game theory versus its extensions in behavioral economics and apply practical strategies in economic decision-making.
Apply social preferences theories to individual, business, and government contexts.

skill_outcomes.skill_name: Critical Reading and Understanding Journal Articles
skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Read and comprehend journal articles using concepts and methods introduced in the course.

Work independently and collaboratively to solve class scenarios and individual assignments. Develop skills for organizing discussions, building scenarios, and presenting real-world situations related to behavioral economics.
Develop abilities for self-study, research, and organizing group activities to complete assigned coursework and projects.
Demonstrate awareness of classroom discipline organization; have a cooperative spirit and sense of responsibility in group activities.
Effectively present and persuade different audiences based on scientific and logical approaches.
